full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent No. 1 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 42 of 1994 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Bheramara, Kushtia stating that the land measuring 3.72 acres in S.A. Khatian No.  880 under mouja Bahirchar in Bheramara Thana was recorded in the name of Rahman for 3/4 share and in the name of Aziz, Saber, Akez, Samer and Azim for 1/4 share. Rahman died leaving his heirs two daughters, Rabia and Achhia. Aziz died leaving behind three nephews, namely, Saber, Samer and Akez. Thereafter, Saber died leaving behind only daughter Robiunnessa if and Samer died leaving behind his son Karban Ali and Akez also died leaving behind his daughter Rejia; that the plaintiffs lived in a joint family along with defendant No. 1 as their guardian and subsequently, they became the owners of the joint property but all those properties were in the name of the defendant No. 1 as he was their guardian. Father of the plaintiffs and defendants, Moksed Ali also got some land by way of bandabasto from the daughter of the C.S. recorded tenant Rahman. Thereafter, Moksed Ali made homestead thereon and had been living thereon by paying rent. Subsequently, the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 bought some land from Karban, Robiunnessa and Rejia in the name of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. They also bought some land from Azimunnessa and Achhia Khatun. Thereafter, their father Moksed Ali died in the year 1989 and they became separate and extended their homestead in those lands and have been possessing the same. Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No.  42 of 1994 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Bheramara, Kushtia and included the plaintiffs as party and subsequently, the plaintiffs came to know that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 bought all those joint property in their names without including the names of the plaintiffs. The defendant No. 1 got his name recorded in the R.S. record. In such condition the plaintiffs claimed .their share from the defendants but the defendants denied. Hence, the suit.
